actuation_contract.order: raw action retained; affine target; absolute joint clipping; encoder-bias correction; actuator latency

com_randomization_contract.effective_at: startup; sampled once per world, retained across resets
com_randomization_contract.scope: density-only pseudo-inertia retaining the already sampled additive body-frame COM offset

collision_contract.scope: Torso contacts terrain and nonadjacent active knee/foot spheres; no lower-leg hulls added. Original masses, sphere geometry and sphere collision properties retained.

protocol.evaluation_contract: Both original and corrected policies evaluated with controller target clamp, composed COM, torso-only contact; no class-driver clamp in these GPU sweeps.
protocol.randomization: Seeded default-play startup physical randomization and observation noise retained despite randomized=False; each before/after pair has byte-identical realized physical randomization snapshots.
protocol.physical_failures_scope: Zero configured failure terminations/timeouts, not evidence of precise commanded speed or hardware suitability.

interpretation: The continuation improves measured velocity/yaw tracking under corrected torso contact, but slow translation remains poor. At seed101, forward0.05m/s yields0.00010m/s, forward0.10m/s yields0.0321m/s, and forward0.15m/s yields0.0807m/s.

The actor requests front knee positions outside controller limits in many states; the configured controller clamp is active. The separate class driver further restricts these same knee targets. No command range is enlarged to hide this.

Corrected torso geometry scored penetration is at most2.24mm, compared with at most3.05mm for the original policy under the SAME corrected contact model. These compliant contacts differ from the prior32.7mm pass-through under a disabled torso.

The policy can support bounded continuous entry/walking/exit experiments after the activation fix, but speed fidelity and physical model mismatch prevent claiming a fully validated Spider walking capability.
next_step: Verify installed driver bounds and robot geometry; then evaluate a separately versioned Spider reference with additional torso/foot clearance and feasible knee targets before another training experiment. Preserve current references and measured comparisons.
